findings.title: Header `.title` float removed and `.contents` made flex, which may break the layout
Invalid or incorrect legacy prefix values in the `align-items` mixin
Small-action spacing changed, and the flex layout may regress

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate: -ms-align-items is not a real property (dead code)
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: that '-ms-align-items' is not a valid/real CSS property. The golden comment provides more detail about what the correct property should be (-ms-flex-align), while the candidate simply notes it's 'not a real property (dead code)'. They are pointing to the same underlying problem - the use of a non-existent vendor-prefixed property.

false_positives.candidate: Header .title float removed and .contents made flex, which may break the layout - other rules for .title may depend on old block/float behaviour
Order values are inconsistent - .panel gets 3, .extra-info-wrapper gets 2, but title has no explicit order (defaults to 0), making ordering fragile
Invalid legacy prefix values in align-items mixin - -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align don't accept flex-start or flex-end values
-moz-box-align is missing from the align-items mixin
Inconsistent indentation and trailing whitespace on line 120 in the mixin
.small-action-desc padding changed to percentage values (0 1.5%), causing spacing to vary with viewport width
Flex items in .small-action may wrap or overflow because they default to min-width: auto - .small-action-desc may need flex: 1 or min-width: 0

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
